newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine cardinal blasts charter change moves.
newsitem.headline: Philippine cardinal blasts charter change moves.

text.p: The Philippine's most influential prelate told Filipinos on Monday to be ready to revive "people power" protests to thwart moves to change the constitution, warning that "tyranny can come step by step."
"What we were were ready to die for in February 1986, we should be ready to fight for again... If need be, we will be there again," Sin said, joining a clamour against revising the constitution.
Sin made his call in a homily at a mass commemorating the 1986 "people power" revolt that toppled then-president Ferdinand Marcos and restored democracy in the Philippines.
Sin played a major role in the uprising by calling out a million Filipinos onto a major highway to surround and protect army mutineers, who included Ramos, against advancing Marcos tanks.
"We gather here to say what we said in '86 - ' Never again! Never again!'" Sin said.
Separately, former Philippine president Corazon Aquino urged President Fidel Ramos to arrange for a peaceful transfer of power to his successor after Sin denounced proposals to extend Ramos's term.
Aquino said she believed Ramos was "very sincere" when he told her at a meeting on Sunday that he would step down when his term ends in June 1998 in order "to give others a chance."
"But I think that what is more important is for the president to provide for us a peaceful and orderly transfer of power on June 30, 1998," she told a meeting of her supporters.

Ramos has repeatedly said he will step down at the end of his six-year tenure, but many have questioned his sincerity after aides revealed that members of his Lakas (People Power) party wanted the constitution changed to permit a second term.
The current constitution, a reaction to Marcos's 20-year rule, limits a president to only one term of six years.
